messages.author: 5914e579c97f1326
messages.subject: Bym 2 model
parts:
I have recently learnt the improvements made in this from from Besag, to BYM and bym2. I want to construct a spatio-temporal model, but my first question is on the spatial part

 In specifying the  bym2 is the structured and unstructured part accounted for in the following ?
formulac<-y~ 1 + f(region.struct1,model="bym2",graph="KEN.adj",scale.model = TRUE, constr=TRUE,  hyper = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.001))))

Or I have to specify the unstructured part as follows 

formulac<-y~ 1 + f(region.struct1,model="bym2",graph="KEN.adj",scale.model = TRUE, constr=TRUE, hyper = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.001))))+
                f(region.unstruct1,model="iid", constr=TRUE)+


And thirdly how to I define to use default PC priors

Thanks 
PM

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Bym 2 model
parts:
Hi & thanks for your email.

The bym2 model is ``the better'' version of the besag+iid, discussed by

author = {A. Riebler and S. H. S{\o}rbye and D. Simpson and H.
Rue},
title = {An intuitive {B}ayesian spatial model for disease
mapping that accounts for scaling},
journal = {Statistical Methods in Medical Research},
year = 2016,
volume = {25},
number = {4},
pages = {1145-1165}
}


inla.doc("bym2") give details.


the model 'bym2' defines both the structured and unstructed term, with
sensisble scaling and corrections for disconnected regions in the
graph.

hence,

formulac<-y~ 1 + f(region.struct1,model="bym2",graph="KEN.adj")

is often sufficient, unless you want to change the priors; see the
documentation.

the PC-priors are default for this model, both for the precision and
for the mixing parameter (which prior is computed at run-time,as it
depends on the graph).

Best
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Bym 2 model
parts:
Hi Rue ,

I have now formulated a space time model, with a type 11 interaction.  Am wondering if I have overlooked anything 
Enter code here...                        
formulac<-y ~ 1 + f(reg0,model="bym2",graph="KEN.adj",constr = TRUE, scale.model = TRUE,hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1,0.01)), phi = list(prior = "pc", param = c(0.5, 0.5)))) +
                            f(time0,model="rw1", constr = TRUE, scale.model = TRUE,hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1,0.01)))) +
                            f(time1, model = "iid", constr = TRUE)+
                            f(reg1,model="iid", group=time2,control.group=list(model="rw1"), constr=TRUE)

                          #Call inla  
                          modc<-inla(formulac,family="gpoisson",data=data,
                                    control.predictor=list(compute=T,link=1),
                                    control.compute = list(dic=TRUE,waic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE),verbose=TRUE)
                         


Thanks 
PM
